candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: Stromal Cav1 expression affects primary tumor growth of LM-4175 breast cancer cells in vivo
candidates.citation_sentence: The comparisons of the primary tumor growth between the three groups of mice, LM-4175 cells injected with or without Cav1WT or Cav1KO pMEFs, which were reported in Figure 2A of this study and Supplemental Figure 7Ca of Goetz et al. (2011), were in the same directions between the two studies and the effect size point estimate of each study was within the CI of the other study (Figure 4A).
candidates.notes: Authors explicitly state primary tumor growth 'does not change when Cav1 is absent in the tumor stroma'; meta-analysis p=0.467; all three planned comparisons non-significant. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: Stromal Cav1 expression increases metastatic burden of LM-4175 breast cancer cells in vivo
candidates.citation_sentence: There were three comparisons of total metastasis formation between the three groups, which was reported in Figure 2C of this study and Figure 7Cb of Goetz et al. (2011).
candidates.notes: Authors summarize metastasis results as 'not in the same direction as the original study and not statistically significant' for the planned comparisons; however, the LM-4175 vs LM-4175 plus Cav1KO meta-analysis was significant (p=0.0027) in the same direction as the original, creating ambiguity. candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: Intratumoral fibronectin fiber alignment is positively correlated with metastatic burden
candidates.citation_sentence: Finally, the rank-order correlation that was determined in both studies to determine the association of fibronectin fiber orientation and total metastasis for all three groups, LM-4175 cells injected with or without Cav1WT or Cav1KO pMEFs, reported in Figure 3C of this study and Figure 7Cd of Goetz et al. (2011), were not consistent when considering direction of the effect (Figure 4D).
candidates.notes: Original reported a statistically significant positive correlation; replication found a statistically significant negative correlation (rs=−0.50, p=0.025); authors explicitly describe results as 'statistically significant in the opposite direction as the original study'; meta-analysis not significant (p=0.837) with significant heterogeneity (Cochran's Q p=2.13×10−5). candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: The original study claimed that Cav1WT primary mouse embryonic fibroblasts have greater extracellular-matrix remodeling and collagen contraction capabilities than Cav1KO fibroblasts; the replication tested this with a collagen gel contraction assay.
candidates.citation_sentence: Although the data were not reported, the original study stated that the ECM remodeling capabilities of Cav1KO pMEFs were reduced compared to Cav1WT pMEFs, similar to the results reported with immortalized MEFs (Goetz et al., 2011).
candidates.notes: The replication found reduced contraction in Cav1KO pMEFs, in the same direction as the original claim. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: The original study reported that stromal Cav1 status does not substantially alter primary tumor growth in mice injected with LM-4175 cells with or without Cav1WT or Cav1KO pMEFs; the replication tested this primary tumor growth outcome.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 7C and Supplemental Figure 7C of Goetz et al. (2011) and described in Protocols 3 and 4 in the Registered Report (Fiering et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found no statistically significant difference in primary tumor growth and interpreted this as suggesting that primary tumor growth does not change when Cav1 is absent from the tumor stroma. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: The original study claimed that Cav1-positive tumor stroma increases metastatic burden compared with Cav1KO stroma or tumor cells without stromal fibroblasts; the replication tested metastatic foci formation in the corresponding mouse groups.
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 7C and Supplemental Figure 7C of Goetz et al. (2011) and described in Protocols 3 and 4 in the Registered Report (Fiering et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication authors reported that metastatic results were not in the same direction as the original study and were not statistically significant. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: The original study claimed that co-injection with Cav1WT fibroblasts increases intratumoral fibronectin fiber alignment relative to tumor cells alone or Cav1KO fibroblasts; the replication measured fibronectin fiber orientation in primary tumors.
candidates.citation_sentence: This compares to the original study that reported a statistically significant increase in fibronectin fiber alignment when LM-4175 cells were co-injected with Cav1WT pMEFs [Mdn = 52.5%, IQR = 43.6–55.4%, n = 8] compared to LM-4175 cells [Mdn = 36.9%, IQR = 36.8–37.7%, n = 5] or LM-4175 plus Cav1KO pMEFs [Mdn = 42.2%, IQR = 40.8–43.2%, n = 10], suggesting stromal Cav1 remodels the intratumoral microenvironment (Goetz et al., 2011).
candidates.notes: The replication effect was in the same direction but not statistically significant, and the analysis workflow differed from the original. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
candidates.description: The original study claimed a positive relationship between intratumoral fibronectin fiber alignment and metastatic burden; the replication tested the correlation between fibronectin fiber orientation and total metastatic foci.
candidates.citation_sentence: The same type of analysis was reported in the original study, which indicated a statistically significant positive relationship (Goetz et al., 2011).
candidates.notes: The replication found a statistically significant relationship in the opposite direction and explicitly summarized the result as opposite to the original study. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

prior_source_review.finding: Descriptions identify the same Cav1 metastasis experiment. The result paragraph reports non-significant, nonmatching direction and a shorter endpoint. This is an interpretation disagreement, not a wrong-original pairing; failure is better supported than calling it a significant reversal.
